test: Pennsylvania Non-Commercial Learner's Permit Knowledge Test (Class C)
edition: Based on the Pennsylvania Driver's Manual, PUB 95 (rev. 4-21), the edition currently linked by PennDOT Driver & Vehicle Services (pa.gov/dmv), checked October 2026; plus PennDOT's 'Pennsylvania Point System' fact sheet (March 2024) and the 2025/2026 handheld-device law (Paul Miller's Law)

exam.rules: Everyone applying for a first Pennsylvania non-commercial learner's permit (age 16 or older; under-18 applicants also need a parent or guardian consent form) takes the same knowledge test at a PennDOT Driver License Center after a vision check. It has 18 multiple-choice questions on traffic signs, Pennsylvania driving laws and safe-driving practices, and you must answer 15 correctly to pass; there is no separately scored sign section. The test is offered in written or audio format and in about 30 languages. You may take it only once per day; if you fail, you can retake it the next business day. Passing earns a learner's permit valid for one year.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a non-commercial learner's permit in Pennsylvania?
questions.explain: You cannot apply for a Pennsylvania learner's permit before your 16th birthday.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Applying for a Learner's Permit'

questions.q: How long is a Pennsylvania learner's permit valid from its issue date?
questions.explain: The learner's permit is valid for one year from the issue date printed on it.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Learner's Permit Information'

questions.q: How many questions are on the Pennsylvania knowledge test for a learner's permit?
questions.explain: The knowledge test has 18 multiple-choice questions.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Tests: Knowledge Test'

questions.q: How many questions must you answer correctly to pass Pennsylvania's knowledge test?
questions.explain: You must answer 15 of the 18 questions correctly (about 83%).
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Tests: Knowledge Test'

questions.q: If you fail the knowledge test, when may you take it again?
options: Later the same day at a different Driver License Center
questions.explain: You may take the knowledge test only once per day at any location; a retake is allowed the next business day.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Tests: Knowledge Test'

questions.q: How many hours of supervised behind-the-wheel practice must a driver under 18 complete before the road test?
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 need at least 65 hours of skill-building, certified by a parent or guardian.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Applying for a Learner's Permit'

questions.q: Of the required practice hours for drivers under 18, how many must be nighttime driving?
questions.explain: The 65 hours must include no less than 10 hours of nighttime driving.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Applying for a Learner's Permit'

questions.q: Of the required practice hours for drivers under 18, how many must be in bad weather?
questions.explain: The 65 hours must include at least 5 hours of bad-weather driving.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Applying for a Learner's Permit'

questions.q: A permit holder under 18 must wait how long after the permit is issued before taking the road test?
questions.explain: There is a mandatory six-month wait from the permit issue date for drivers under 18.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Applying for a Learner's Permit'

questions.q: Who may supervise a learner's permit holder under 18?
options: A licensed driver at least 21, or a licensed parent, guardian or spouse who is at least 18
Any passenger at least 25, licensed or not
questions.explain: A supervisor must hold a license and be 21+, unless they are the learner's licensed parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse, who need only be 18+.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Learner's Permit Information'

questions.q: Where must the supervising driver sit when a permit holder under 18 is driving?
options: In the rear seat on the passenger side
questions.explain: The supervising driver must ride in the front seat at all times.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Learner's Permit Information'

questions.q: During which hours may a junior licensee NOT drive unless accompanied by a parent, guardian or spouse 18 or older (or covered by a work/volunteer exception)?
questions.explain: From 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. a junior licensee may drive only with a parent, guardian or spouse (18+) aboard, or under the work/volunteer exception.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Driver's License Information'

questions.q: A junior licensee who must drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. for a job or volunteer fire company must carry:
options: A note from any licensed adult
A notarized affidavit or certificate from the employer, supervisor or fire chief
A letter from a school principal
questions.explain: For late-night work or volunteer duty, keep a notarized affidavit or authorization certificate from the employer, supervisor or fire chief listing your expected schedule with your license.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Driver's License Information'

questions.q: During the first six months on a junior license, how many passengers under 18 who are not immediate family may ride with you without a parent or guardian present?
questions.explain: For the first six months, no more than one non-family passenger under 18 is allowed unless a parent, guardian or spouse 18+ is in the vehicle.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Driver's License Information'

questions.q: After six months on a junior license with no at-fault crash or conviction, the limit on non-family passengers under 18 rises to:
questions.explain: The limit increases to three non-family passengers under 18 unless the driver has had an at-fault crash or a driving conviction.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Driver's License Information'

questions.q: For drivers under 18, how many passengers may be in the vehicle?
options: No more than the number of seat belts in the vehicle
Any number if a parent is present
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 may not carry more passengers than there are seat belts.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Seat Belt Law'

questions.q: A junior driver will receive a 90-day suspension for a first occurrence of which of the following?
options: Building up 6 or more points or being convicted of driving 26 mph or more over the limit
questions.explain: Drivers under 18 are suspended for 90 days for 6+ points or a conviction for driving 26+ mph over the posted limit.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'The Pennsylvania Point System'

questions.q: For a driver under 18, how long is the suspension for a second occurrence of 6+ points or driving 26+ mph over the limit?
questions.explain: The first suspension is 90 days; any additional occurrence results in a 120-day suspension.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'The Pennsylvania Point System'

questions.q: When does a Pennsylvania junior driver's license automatically become a regular license?
options: After passing a second road test
questions.explain: A junior license automatically becomes a regular license at age 18.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Driver's License Information'

questions.q: Which is a requirement for converting a junior license to a regular license before age 18?
options: Holding the junior license for 3 months
Holding the junior license 12 months and passing an approved driver training course
questions.explain: You also need no at-fault crash or conviction for one year and parental consent.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Junior Driver's License Information'

questions.q: If a driver under 18 fails the road test, how long must they wait to retake it?
questions.explain: Pennsylvania law requires drivers under 18 to wait seven days before retaking the road test.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Tests: Road Test'

questions.q: How many chances to pass the road test do you get with each learner's permit?
questions.explain: Each permit allows three road-test attempts; after a third failure you must apply (form DL-31) to extend the permit.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Tests: Road Test'

questions.q: A new Pennsylvania resident with a valid license from another state must get a Pennsylvania license within:
questions.explain: New residents must obtain a Pennsylvania license within 60 days and surrender the out-of-state license.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 1 (Learner's Permit Information), section 'Who Needs a Pennsylvania Driver's License?'

questions.q: How soon must you notify PennDOT after changing your name or address?
questions.explain: Section 1515 of the Vehicle Code requires notifying PennDOT within 15 days.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Required Notification for Change in Name or Address'

questions.q: How often must a Pennsylvania-registered passenger vehicle pass a safety inspection?
questions.explain: A safety inspection is required every 12 months; it may be done up to 90 days early.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Vehicle Safety and Emissions Inspection'

questions.q: What must you do at this sign?
options: Slow down and go if no one is coming
Stop only if cross traffic is present
Come to a complete stop, then go when the way is clear
questions.explain: Slowing without a full stop is illegal; stop, check for pedestrians and cross traffic, then proceed when clear.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Slow down and give the right-of-way to pedestrians and cross traffic, stopping if necessary
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Keep going; other traffic must yield to you
questions.explain: At a YIELD sign you slow, check traffic, and stop only when necessary.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: Where would you normally see this sign?
options: At the start of a school zone
At the entrance to a one-way street or ramp you must not enter
At the end of a divided highway
questions.explain: This sign marks the entry point of a one-way street or ramp that traffic is not allowed to enter from your direction.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: If you see this sign, what has happened?
options: You are in a high-occupancy lane
You have entered a work zone
You are traveling against traffic on a one-way road or ramp
questions.explain: WRONG WAY signs are placed farther down a one-way street or ramp to warn drivers who entered by mistake.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: 55 mph is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions
55 mph is only a recommended speed for trucks
questions.explain: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; drive slower when conditions are poor.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Left turns allowed only on green
Left turns are not allowed at this intersection
questions.explain: A black left arrow in a red circle with a slash prohibits left turns.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not turn around to go in the opposite direction
questions.explain: This sign prohibits U-turns.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign, what must you do while your signal is red?
options: Wait for a green signal before turning
Stop, then turn right if clear
Turn only if no pedestrians are present
questions.explain: With this sign present, no turn of any kind is permitted while the signal is red; wait for green.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic may move only in the direction of the arrow
Detour in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: The arrow shows the only direction traffic may travel on this street.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not pass vehicles traveling in your direction
Do not stop on the shoulder
questions.explain: DO NOT PASS marks areas where passing vehicles going your way is not allowed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: When the round green signal is lit at an intersection with this sign, you may turn left:
options: Never; wait for a green arrow
With the right-of-way over oncoming traffic
Only after yielding to oncoming traffic
questions.explain: LEFT TURN YIELD ON GREEN reminds drivers that left turns are not protected on a circular green.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: Which vehicles may park in a space marked with this sign?
options: Any vehicle for up to 15 minutes
Vehicles displaying a disability plate or placard and carrying or driven by the person with a disability
Any vehicle with hazard lights on
questions.explain: Two conditions apply: the vehicle shows a disability plate or placard, and it is being used by or to transport the person with the disability.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Parking Areas for Persons with Disabilities'

questions.q: How should you treat this sign?
options: Like a YIELD sign: slow down and be ready to stop for a train
As a warning that tracks are no longer used
Like a STOP sign every time
questions.explain: A crossbuck works like a YIELD sign: slow, look and listen, and stop if a train is coming.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: At a STOP sign with this plate underneath, two cars arrive at the same time from different roads. Who goes first?
options: The driver going straight, regardless of side
questions.explain: At an all-way stop the first vehicle there goes first; when two arrive together, the one on the left lets the one on the right go.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: You are in a lane under this sign. What must you do at the intersection?
options: Go straight if the way is clear
Turn in the direction of the arrow, even if you entered the lane by mistake
questions.explain: In a lane with an arrow and the word ONLY, you must make the turn shown.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Lane Use Control Signs'

questions.q: What does this warning sign tell you?
options: The road curves to the right ahead
Side road enters from the right
questions.explain: On a right curve, slow down and keep slightly right of lane center.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: How should you respond to this sign?
options: Keep your speed; it is a gentle curve
Slow down substantially for a sharp right turn ahead
Prepare to turn onto a side road
questions.explain: The road ahead turns sharply right; slow down substantially and keep slightly right of lane center.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: This sign is posted on a major road. What does it mean?
options: Traffic may merge into your lane from the right
questions.explain: Vehicles may be joining from the right; they must yield to you, but be ready to adjust speed or position to let them in safely.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should drivers in the right lane do when they see this sign?
options: Prepare to merge left because the right lane ends
Nothing; it applies only to trucks
questions.explain: LANE ENDS signs warn that one lane ends and its traffic must merge.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A divided highway begins ahead; keep right of the median
questions.explain: The highway becomes two one-way roadways separated by a median; keep to the right of the divider.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Slow down and be ready to stop for a traffic light you may not yet see
Speed up to beat the light
questions.explain: A traffic signal is ahead, possibly hidden by a curve or hill, and traffic may be stopped.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A school bus stop is ahead
A STOP sign is ahead and may be hidden from view
questions.explain: STOP AHEAD warns of a stop sign around a curve or hill; slow down to prepare to stop.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign in wet weather?
options: Reduce speed, increase following distance, and avoid quick braking
questions.explain: SLIPPERY WHEN WET: slow down, increase following distance and avoid sudden braking or acceleration.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: This five-sided sign means:
options: You are approaching a school zone; slow down and watch for children
questions.explain: The pentagon is the only five-sided roadway sign and marks a school zone.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: When you see this round sign, you should:
options: Begin looking and listening for a train
questions.explain: The railroad advance sign is placed far enough ahead to let you stop before the tracks if needed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: This pennant-shaped sign is placed on which side of the road?
options: The left side, facing the driver
On the median only for trucks
questions.explain: The NO PASSING ZONE pennant is the only pennant-shaped sign and is posted on the left side of the road.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: A yellow plate like this under a curve sign tells you:
options: The legal speed limit for the whole road
The highest safe speed for the curve under good conditions
questions.explain: Advisory speed plates may be used with diamond-shaped warning signs to show a safe speed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs: Advisory Speed Signs'

questions.q: What do orange signs like this indicate?
options: Construction, maintenance or utility work ahead
questions.explain: Work zone signs are orange with black letters; slow down and stay alert.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Work Zone Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: A flagger is controlling traffic ahead
questions.explain: Flaggers use STOP/SLOW paddles or red flags; their directions must be obeyed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Work Zone Signs'

questions.q: This orange triangle with a red border on the back of a vehicle means the vehicle:
options: Is designed to travel at 25 mph or less
questions.explain: The slow-moving vehicle emblem appears on farm tractors and horse-drawn vehicles that operate at 25 mph or less.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Reactions to Slow Moving Traffic'

questions.q: What is the only eight-sided sign used on Pennsylvania roads?
questions.explain: The STOP sign is the only octagon-shaped sign.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: Warning signs are usually what shape and color?
questions.explain: Most warning signs are yellow diamonds with black symbols or words.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What must you do when facing this steady signal?
options: Turn left onto a two-way street after slowing
Stop at the stop line or crosswalk and wait for green, unless a legal turn on red is allowed
Slow down and proceed without stopping
Stop, then drive straight through if no cars are coming
questions.explain: On steady red you must stop before the stop line or crosswalk; a right turn (or left from one-way to one-way) after stopping is allowed unless prohibited.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Red, Yellow and Green Traffic Lights'

questions.q: You are approaching the intersection and this light appears. You can stop safely. What should you do?
options: Stop in the middle of the intersection
Speed up to clear the intersection
questions.explain: A steady yellow means red is coming; stop if you can do so safely.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Red, Yellow and Green Traffic Lights'

questions.q: When this arrow is lit, your left turn is:
options: Allowed only after a full stop
Allowed only after yielding to oncoming traffic
Protected, because oncoming traffic has a red light
questions.explain: A steady green arrow gives a protected turn in the arrow's direction.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Red, Yellow and Green Traffic Lights'

questions.q: This flashing signal has the same meaning as:
questions.explain: Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Flashing Signals'

questions.q: What does this flashing signal mean?
options: The signal is broken; treat as a four-way stop
Slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light means caution.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Flashing Signals'

questions.q: A flashing yellow arrow means you may turn in the arrow's direction:
options: Only if no traffic light is red
After yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explain: Turns on a flashing yellow arrow are not protected; oncoming traffic has a green light.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Flashing Signals'

questions.q: How should you treat a traffic signal that is not working at all?
options: As a green light for the main road
questions.explain: A non-functioning signal is treated as a four-way stop.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Non-Functioning Traffic Lights'

questions.q: Yellow centerlines separate:
options: Traffic moving in the same direction
questions.explain: Yellow lines divide opposing traffic; white lines divide lanes going the same way.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: What does this marking in the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: Passing is not allowed in either direction
Passing allowed only for the side nearest the line
questions.explain: A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing from either direction, even without a sign.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: This single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road means:
options: Passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe
questions.explain: A single broken yellow centerline allows passing on either side when safe, using the oncoming lane.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: With this marking, the broken yellow line is on your side. What does that mean?
options: Only the other side may pass
You may pass when it is safe
You may pass only on the right
questions.explain: You may pass when the broken line is on your side; you may not when the solid line is on your side.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: Broken white lines like these separate:
options: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, which may be crossed when safe
questions.explain: Broken white lines mark lanes for the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: A center lane marked like this on both sides is used for:
options: Left turns by traffic from either direction
questions.explain: A solid outer and broken inner yellow line mark a center lane only for left turns.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Turning From or Into a Center Turn Lane'

questions.q: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time from different roads, which must yield?
options: The driver on the right yields
The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right
questions.explain: With no signs or signals, when two vehicles reach the intersection together, the vehicle on the right goes first.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:
options: No one, if your signal is on
questions.explain: A left turn crosses oncoming traffic, so the turning driver waits for oncoming straight-through vehicles.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: A driver entering a roundabout must yield to:
options: No one; entering traffic has priority
Vehicles waiting to enter from the right
questions.explain: Entering drivers yield to circulating traffic, which has the right-of-way.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Circular Intersections'

questions.q: Traffic in a roundabout travels:
questions.explain: Roundabout traffic circulates counterclockwise, which makes every entry and exit a right turn.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Circular Intersections'

questions.q: As you approach your exit in a roundabout, you should:
options: Stop in the circle to check traffic
Use your right turn signal and watch for pedestrians
questions.explain: Signal right as you approach your exit and be prepared to yield to pedestrians.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Circular Intersections'

questions.q: An emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout. You should:
options: Exit the roundabout and then pull over
Speed up to stay ahead of it
questions.explain: Never stop in a roundabout; exit and pull to the side.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Circular Intersections'

questions.q: A vehicle entering a public road from a driveway, alley or private road must:
options: Wait until the main road is clear
Merge at the speed of traffic without stopping
questions.explain: Traffic coming out of a driveway, alley or private road waits for a clear gap; vehicles on the main road go first.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: At a four-way stop, which vehicle should go first?
options: The first vehicle to reach the intersection
questions.explain: All vehicles stop; the first to arrive proceeds first.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: At a four-way stop, two vehicles facing each other arrive at the same time. What should happen?
options: Both must wait for a third vehicle
The one turning left goes first
The one on the left goes first
Both may proceed with caution, watching for turns
questions.explain: Drivers facing each other may both proceed carefully, watching for possible turns.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: You must yield to pedestrians:
options: In marked crosswalks and at intersections without traffic lights, even with no marked crosswalk
Only when a signal shows WALK
questions.explain: Drivers yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without signals (marked or not) and in marked crosswalks.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: When you cross a sidewalk while leaving a driveway or alley, you must:
options: Yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to pedestrians walking on a sidewalk that crosses a driveway or alley.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: A pedestrian is carrying a white cane or using a guide dog. You must:
options: Proceed if they are not in your lane
Honk so they know you are there
Always yield the right-of-way and be ready to stop
questions.explain: Drivers must always yield to blind pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Pedestrian Signals: Blind Pedestrians'

questions.q: According to the manual, right-of-way law:
options: Only says who must yield; it does not give anyone the right-of-way
Lets you insist on your turn
questions.explain: Even when another driver should yield, you must still stop or yield as needed to avoid a crash.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Intersections'

questions.q: When you hear a siren or see an emergency vehicle with flashing red (or red and blue) lights approaching, you must:
options: Pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop
Speed up to clear the way
questions.explain: Pull over and stop, staying clear of intersections.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Emergency Vehicles and Situations'

questions.q: On a one-way street, when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you should:
options: Keep driving until the next intersection
Pull toward the nearest roadside and stop
questions.explain: On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Emergency Vehicles and Situations'

questions.q: After an emergency vehicle passes you, how far behind it must you stay?
questions.explain: Resume driving after it passes, keeping at least 500 feet away.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Emergency Vehicles and Situations'

questions.q: Who must you yield to in a highway work zone?
options: No one; through traffic has priority
questions.explain: In work zones, workers and construction equipment have priority; slow down and give way.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Work Zones'

questions.q: A flagger's directions conflict with a traffic signal in a work zone. You should follow:
questions.explain: A flagger's authority overrides conventional traffic control devices.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Work Zones'

questions.q: In a short weaving lane between a highway entrance and exit, who must yield?
options: The driver entering the highway yields to the driver exiting
questions.explain: If you are entering, yield to the exiting driver.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Entering Highways'

questions.q: A funeral procession is passing through an intersection. Other drivers must:
options: Yield and not cut into the procession
Join the end of the procession
Pass the procession on the right
questions.explain: Once the lead vehicle has cleared the intersection, the procession may continue and other traffic must yield.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Funeral Procession'

questions.q: Vehicles in a funeral procession must yield to:
questions.explain: Funeral processions must yield to emergency vehicles.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Funeral Procession'

questions.q: You are stopped at a STOP sign and your view of cross traffic is blocked. What should you do?
options: Back up and choose another route
After stopping, creep forward slowly until you can see clearly, then go when clear
questions.explain: Stop before the line, yield to pedestrians, then pull forward carefully until you can see.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: When a vehicle is entering the highway from an on-ramp next to you, the entering driver:
options: Must stop at the end of the ramp
Must yield to traffic already on the highway
questions.explain: Entering traffic must yield; changing lanes to help them merge is a courtesy if it is safe.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Traveling on Highways'

questions.q: With a green light, you see traffic backed up beyond the intersection. You should:
options: Enter and wait in the intersection
Wait until you can clear the intersection before entering
Turn on hazard lights and enter
questions.explain: Do not enter an intersection, even on green, if vehicles block your way.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Crossing Traffic'

questions.q: What is the maximum speed limit allowed anywhere in Pennsylvania?
questions.explain: The maximum speed limit in Pennsylvania is 70 mph where posted.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Posted Speed Limits'

questions.q: What is the speed limit in a school zone when the yellow lights on the school zone sign are flashing?
questions.explain: You must drive no faster than 15 mph when the lights flash or during posted times.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'School Zone Signals'

questions.q: How many points are added for exceeding the school zone speed limit?
questions.explain: Speeding in a school zone results in 3 points and a fine.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'School Zone Signals'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a Pennsylvania urban district?
questions.explain: The Vehicle Code sets 35 mph in urban districts unless a different limit is posted.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Vehicle Code, 75 Pa.C.S. §3362 (maximum speed limits)

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, the general maximum speed on Pennsylvania roads outside urban districts (other than posted freeways) is:
questions.explain: The Vehicle Code's default maximum for other locations is 55 mph.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Vehicle Code, 75 Pa.C.S. §3362 (maximum speed limits)

questions.q: What following distance does the Pennsylvania manual recommend on dry pavement?
questions.explain: A 4-second following distance lets you steer or brake to avoid a hazard on dry pavement.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Keep a Space Cushion Ahead (4-Second Rule)'

questions.q: On wet roads, the manual says to reduce speed by 5 to 10 mph and increase following distance to:
questions.explain: Slow 5–10 mph on wet roads and allow 5–6 seconds of following distance.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Snow and Ice'

questions.q: On packed snow, you should reduce your speed by about:
questions.explain: Cut your speed roughly in half on packed snow, and to a crawl on ice.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Snow and Ice'

questions.q: On ice- or snow-covered roads, how much space should you leave compared with normal?
questions.explain: Leave about 10 times more space than normal on ice or snow.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Snow and Ice'

questions.q: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as:
questions.explain: You can hydroplane at 35 mph on water only 1/10 of an inch deep.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Hydroplaning'

questions.q: Roads are often most slippery:
options: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm
Only when temperatures are below freezing
After it has rained for several hours
Right after the rain stops and the road dries
questions.explain: Rain brings oil in the asphalt to the surface early in a storm.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Wet Pavements'

questions.q: Low-beam headlights light the road about how far ahead?
questions.explain: Low beams shine only about 250 feet, less than the stopping distance at 55 mph.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving at Night'

questions.q: To avoid overdriving your low-beam headlights on a dark road, you should not drive faster than about:
questions.explain: Stopping from 55 mph takes more than 250 feet, so the manual advises 45 mph or less.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving at Night'

questions.q: Can you be ticketed for driving too fast even when you are under the posted limit?
options: No, the posted limit is always legal
Yes, if your speed is too fast for conditions
questions.explain: You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Managing Speed'

questions.q: What is the No. 1 reason 16- and 17-year-old Pennsylvania drivers are involved in crashes?
questions.explain: The manual lists driving too fast for conditions as the top crash factor for teen drivers.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Regulatory Signs: Teen Crash Fact'

questions.q: On a limited-access highway, if you must drive below 40 mph you should:
options: Stop on the shoulder every mile
questions.explain: Use hazard flashers to warn drivers behind you when going below 40 mph on a limited-access highway.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Communicating Your Intentions to Other Drivers'

questions.q: How fast must you be going to safely pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road?
options: About 10 mph faster than the vehicle you are passing
At least 20 mph over the speed limit
questions.explain: A safe pass needs about a 10 mph speed advantage over the vehicle being passed, without exceeding the limit.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing: On a Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: At 45 mph, about how much clear road do you need to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road?
questions.explain: At 45 mph you need about a quarter mile of clear roadway.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing: On a Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: How far ahead should you scan to spot problems early?
options: Only to the vehicle in front
questions.explain: Look 12 to 15 seconds ahead: roughly a city block, or about a quarter mile on the highway.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Looking Ahead'

questions.q: A passenger car traveling 65 mph on a dry road needs about how much distance to stop, according to the manual?
questions.explain: A passenger vehicle needs about 400 feet; a loaded truck needs about 600 feet.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Sharing the Road with Trucks and Buses: Braking'

questions.q: Speeding 6 to 10 mph over the limit adds how many points to your record?
questions.explain: Points for speeding: 6–10 mph over = 2; 11–15 = 3; 16–25 = 4; 26+ = 5.
questions.ref: PennDOT fact sheet 'The Pennsylvania Point System' (March 2024)

questions.q: Speeding 16 to 25 mph over the limit adds how many points?
questions.explain: 16–25 mph over the limit carries 4 points.
questions.ref: PennDOT fact sheet 'The Pennsylvania Point System' (March 2024)

questions.q: A driver convicted of speeding 31 mph or more over the limit faces:
questions.explain: 31+ mph over brings 5 points and a Departmental Hearing with possible sanctions.
questions.ref: PennDOT fact sheet 'The Pennsylvania Point System' (March 2024)

questions.q: When driving under 35 mph, how far before a turn must you signal?
questions.explain: Under 35 mph, signal at least 100 feet before turning.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Communicating Your Intentions to Other Drivers'

questions.q: When driving 35 mph or faster, how far before a turn must you signal?
questions.explain: At 35 mph or more, signal at least 300 feet before turning.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Communicating Your Intentions to Other Drivers'

questions.q: The manual's step-by-step turn guidance says to signal how long before you turn?
options: Only as you begin to turn
questions.explain: Signal three to four seconds before your turn.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'To Complete a Turn Safely'

questions.q: On a two-lane, two-way road, where should you make a left turn from?
options: The right edge of the road
As close to the centerline as possible
questions.explain: Make left turns from close to the centerline and right turns close to the right edge.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Left and Right Turns'

questions.q: When turning onto a road with more than one lane in your direction, you should turn into:
options: The closest lane going in your direction
questions.explain: Turn into the nearest lane; change lanes only after completing the turn.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Left and Right Turns'

questions.q: When may you turn right on a steady red light in Pennsylvania?
options: After stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
Without stopping if no one is coming
questions.explain: Stop, yield to pedestrians and traffic, then turn unless NO TURN ON RED is posted.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Turning Right at a Red Light'

questions.q: A left turn on a steady red light is allowed only when:
options: Turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding
questions.explain: Left on red is only legal from a one-way street into another one-way street, after a full stop and yielding, and not where a sign forbids it.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Red, Yellow and Green Traffic Lights'

questions.q: When choosing a place to make a U-turn, vehicles from all directions should be at least how far away?
questions.explain: Make sure other drivers are at least 500 feet away and can see you clearly.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'U-Turns'

questions.q: U-turns are not allowed:
options: On curves or near the crest of a hill
questions.explain: U-turns are illegal on curves or when approaching or near the top of a hill.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'U-Turns'

questions.q: You may NOT pass another vehicle when you are within how many feet of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge or tunnel?
questions.explain: No passing within 100 feet of intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, elevated structures or tunnels.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing: You May Not Pass If'

questions.q: Before returning to your lane after passing, you should be able to see:
options: The passed vehicle in your side mirror only
Both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
The passed vehicle beside your door
questions.explain: Return only when both headlights of the vehicle you passed appear in your rearview mirror.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing'

questions.q: When may you pass on the right?
options: When the vehicle ahead is turning left, or on roads with two or more marked lanes in your direction
Whenever the shoulder is wide enough
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed in these limited situations; never use a multi-lane highway shoulder to pass.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing on the Right'

questions.q: Passing is most dangerous at night because:
options: You cannot see as far and distances are harder to judge
questions.explain: At night, oncoming headlights can make a vehicle seem farther away than it is.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing: On a Two-Lane Road'

questions.q: Which of these is illegal on an acceleration lane?
options: Passing the vehicle ahead of you
questions.explain: Passing the car ahead while still in the acceleration lane is against the law.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Merging with Traffic'

questions.q: What are the three steps to merge from an acceleration lane?
options: Sound the horn, merge, then signal
Stop at the end, wait, then go
Signal and look for a gap, accelerate to traffic speed, merge into the gap
questions.explain: Signal, match the speed of traffic, then merge into the opening.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Merging with Traffic'

questions.q: You missed your highway exit. What should you do?
options: Stop and wait for a gap to back up
Cross the median to turn around
questions.explain: Never stop, back up or cross the median on a highway; take the next exit.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Exiting Highways'

questions.q: When using a center two-way left-turn lane, you should:
options: Enter it completely and not drive in it too long
Use it to pass slow traffic
Leave your rear sticking into the travel lane
questions.explain: The longer you drive in the center lane, the more likely you are to meet someone head-on.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Turning From or Into a Center Turn Lane'

questions.q: You are in a lane marked for through traffic but wanted to turn. You must:
options: Stop and wait for a gap
Back up into the turn lane
questions.explain: If you are in a through lane, continue straight; if in a turn-only lane, you must turn.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Signs and Pavement Markings for Lane Assignment'

questions.q: To turn left onto a divided highway, you should:
options: Turn left into the first roadway
Turn right and make a U-turn
Cross the first roadway, then turn left into the far roadway past the median
questions.explain: A divided highway is two one-way roads; turning left too soon puts you into oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'One Way, Wrong Way and Do Not Enter Signs'

questions.q: To cross a two-way stop-controlled intersection with a 30 mph cross street, you need about what gap in both directions?
questions.explain: Allow about a 6-second gap, about a block of clear space each way.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Moving Into and Through Intersections Safely'

questions.q: When turning left from a minor street onto a major street, allow a gap of about how long from vehicles approaching from the right?
questions.explain: The manual recommends a 9-second gap for this left turn.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Moving Into and Through Intersections Safely'

questions.q: At an intersection, which way should you look first before pulling out?
options: Left, then right, then left again
questions.explain: Vehicles from the left are closer to you, so look left first and again before pulling out.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Looking to the Sides'

questions.q: Before changing lanes, you should check your blind spots by:
options: Looking over your shoulder in the direction you are moving
questions.explain: Do not rely on mirrors or sensors alone; turn your head to check blind spots quickly.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Looking Behind'

questions.q: On highways, when changing lanes to pass, you should:
options: Change one lane at a time, signaling each time
Skip the signal if no one is near
Signal only once for multiple lanes
questions.explain: Change one lane at a time and use your signal every time.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Traveling on Highways'

questions.q: If your turn signals do not work, how do you signal a left turn by hand?
options: Right arm out the passenger window
Extend your left arm straight out the window
questions.explain: Left arm straight out for left; up for right; down for slowing or stopping.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Hand Signals'

questions.q: A hand signal with your left arm bent upward at the elbow means:
questions.explain: Left arm angled up signals a right turn.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Hand Signals'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
questions.explain: Never park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
questions.explain: Keep at least 20 feet back from a crosswalk at an intersection when parking.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign or flashing signal at the side of the road?
questions.explain: Stay at least 30 feet from these roadside traffic control devices.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail is prohibited.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a fire station driveway entrance?
questions.explain: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway entrance.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: When parking next to a curb, your wheels must be no more than how far from it?
questions.explain: Park as close as you can to the curb, but no more than 12 inches away.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: When parking downhill next to a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
questions.explain: Downhill, with or without a curb, turn the wheels to the right.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'How to Park Your Vehicle on a Hill'

questions.q: When parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: Toward the curb only if the hill is steep
questions.explain: Uphill with a curb, turn the wheels left so the tire rests against the curb if the car rolls.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'How to Park Your Vehicle on a Hill'

questions.q: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: To the right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explain: Without a curb, uphill or downhill, turn the wheels to the right.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'How to Park Your Vehicle on a Hill'

questions.q: Which of these is a place where you may never park (except in an emergency or when directed by police)?
options: On a residential street at night
On a bridge or in a highway tunnel
questions.explain: Bridges, elevated structures and tunnels are no-parking locations.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: Stopping on the roadway side of a vehicle that is already parked at the curb is called:
options: Double parking, and it is not allowed
Standing, and it is allowed for 5 minutes
questions.explain: Double parking is prohibited except in emergencies or as directed by police.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: If you must park on the roadway, your vehicle should be visible from at least how far in both directions?
questions.explain: Use four-way flashers and make sure the vehicle can be seen 500 feet in both directions.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: Which direction must you face when parking on the street?
questions.explain: Always park in the direction traffic moves.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Parking'

questions.q: What is the fine for illegally parking in a space for persons with disabilities?
questions.explain: This summary offense carries a $50–$200 fine, and the vehicle may be towed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Parking Areas for Persons with Disabilities'

questions.q: Before getting out of your parked car on the street side, you should:
options: Check for traffic and bicyclists behind you
questions.explain: Check traffic before getting out; using your far hand (the 'Dutch Reach') helps you see approaching cyclists.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'The Danger of Open Doors to Bicyclists'

questions.q: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and stop arm extended, how far away must you stop?
questions.explain: Stop at least 10 feet from the bus, whether behind it, facing it or at an intersection where it is stopped.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: Amber (yellow) flashing lights on a school bus mean:
options: The bus is preparing to stop; slow down and get ready to stop
questions.explain: Amber lights begin flashing when the bus is preparing to stop.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: When must you NOT stop for a school bus with red lights flashing?
options: When you are behind the bus on a two-lane road
When you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median or barrier
When you are on a four-lane road with no median
questions.explain: The only exception is the opposite side of a divided highway separated by a barrier or median; slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: What is the penalty for failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm?
options: 60-day license suspension, 5 points and a fine
A warning on the first offense
questions.explain: Failure to stop results in a 60-day suspension, 5 points and a fine.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: After a school bus turns off its red lights, you may go when:
options: The red lights turn off, even if children are still crossing
The bus driver waves you on
The stop arm is withdrawn and the children have reached a safe place
questions.explain: Remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, the arm is withdrawn, and children are safe.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: When passing a bicyclist, Pennsylvania law requires at least how much space?
questions.explain: Allow at least four feet; you may cross a double yellow line to do so if it is safe.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Safe Passing is the Law'

questions.q: To give a bicyclist the required space, may you cross a double yellow centerline?
options: Yes, if it can be done safely
questions.explain: Pennsylvania permits crossing the double yellow when necessary and safe to keep 4 feet of clearance.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Safe Passing is the Law'

questions.q: Which statement about bicyclists in Pennsylvania is correct?
options: They may ride below the minimum speed and are not required to use the shoulder
They must always ride on the shoulder
questions.explain: Cyclists are vehicle operators, may travel below minimum speeds and may use, but need not use, the shoulder.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Safe Passing is the Law'

questions.q: How much of a lane does a motorcycle or moped have a right to use?
options: None; it must use the shoulder
questions.explain: Allow the motorcyclist a full lane; do not share it.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Motorcyclists and Moped Drivers'

questions.q: Most crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when:
options: A car turns left in front of a motorcycle at an intersection
questions.explain: Most motorcycle/vehicle crashes occur at intersections, usually a car turning left in front of the rider.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Motorcyclists and Moped Drivers'

questions.q: A motorcycle's turn signal is flashing as it approaches. You should:
options: Wait until you see it actually turn before you pull out
questions.explain: Motorcycle signals may not cancel automatically.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Motorcyclists and Moped Drivers'

questions.q: When following a truck, if you cannot see the truck's side mirrors:
options: You are at a safe distance
The driver can see you on camera
The truck driver cannot see you
questions.explain: If you cannot see the mirrors of a large vehicle, its driver cannot see you.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Following a Truck'

questions.q: After passing a truck, when is it safe to move back in front of it?
options: When you can see the truck's front (headlights or grille) in your rearview mirror
As soon as your rear bumper clears its cab
questions.explain: Cutting in too soon leaves the truck driver little room to stop.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing a Truck'

questions.q: At highway speeds, how long can it take to safely pass a truck?
questions.explain: Allow plenty of time: passing a truck can take up to 30 seconds.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passing a Truck'

questions.q: A loaded truck at 65 mph on dry pavement needs at least how far to stop?
questions.explain: A loaded truck needs about 600 feet compared with about 400 feet for a car.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Braking'

questions.q: A truck ahead signals a right turn but swings left first. You should:
options: Stay back and not try to pass on its right
questions.explain: Trucks make wide right turns; drivers cannot see vehicles squeezing between them and the curb.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Turns'

questions.q: When a truck is passing you, you can help by:
options: Keeping to the far side of your lane and not speeding up
questions.explain: Reduce speed slightly and hold steady; never speed up while being passed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Truck Passing'

questions.q: When stopped behind a truck on an uphill, you should:
options: Leave extra room because it may roll back
Pull up close to its bumper
questions.explain: Trucks may roll back as the driver releases the brake.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Following a Truck'

questions.q: You should never attempt to pass a snowplow:
options: On the left or on the right
Unless it is on a highway
questions.explain: Plows may have wing blades extending several feet and drivers have limited visibility.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Snow Plows'

questions.q: When passing a horse-drawn vehicle or horseback rider, you should:
options: Pass slowly without honking and leave plenty of space before returning to the lane
questions.explain: Speed and horns can spook horses; leave room before pulling back into the right lane.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Horse-Drawn Vehicles and Horseback Riders'

questions.q: Why should you leave extra room when stopped behind a horse-drawn buggy?
options: Buggies often roll backward after stopping
It is required only at night
questions.explain: Horse-drawn vehicles often roll back after stopping.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Horse-Drawn Vehicles and Horseback Riders'

questions.q: An open-bed pickup carrying a person in the bed may not be driven faster than:
questions.explain: With anyone in the bed, the speed limit for the truck is 35 mph.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passengers in an Open-Bed Truck'

questions.q: In general, may a child under 18 ride in the open bed of a pickup truck in Pennsylvania?
options: No, except for limited farm, hunting and parade exceptions
questions.explain: A truck may not be driven with a child under 18 in the bed, with narrow exceptions.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Passengers in an Open-Bed Truck'

questions.q: When approaching a stopped vehicle from behind at a crosswalk, you should:
options: Pass it on the left quickly
Slow and not pass until you are sure no pedestrians are crossing in front of it
questions.explain: A stopped vehicle may be hiding a pedestrian.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: A pedestrian is waiting to cross mid-block. Should you wave them across in front of other traffic?
options: No, it is never safe to wave a pedestrian into traffic
Yes, if you flash your lights
questions.explain: Waving a pedestrian into traffic is never safe, especially at unmarked or mid-block locations.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: After passing a bicyclist, you should:
options: Brake to let them know you passed
Avoid slowing or stopping suddenly in front of them
questions.explain: A quick stop could cause the cyclist to crash into your vehicle.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Following distance behind a motorcycle should be at least:
options: The same as behind a bicycle: 2 feet
4 seconds, and more in bad conditions
questions.explain: Allow at least the same 4 seconds you give other vehicles, more when conditions are poor.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Motorcyclists and Moped Drivers'

questions.q: When must you turn on your headlights in Pennsylvania?
options: Whenever your wipers are on because of weather
questions.explain: One of the headlight rules: if weather has your wipers running (steadily or on intermittent), your headlights must be on.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Headlight/Windshield Wiper Law'

questions.q: Headlights are required whenever you cannot see pedestrians or vehicles how far ahead?
questions.explain: Use headlights when you cannot see people or vehicles 1,000 feet ahead.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving at Night'

questions.q: Are daytime running lights alone enough when headlights are required?
options: No, your taillights must also be on
questions.explain: Daytime running lights are not enough; tail lights must be illuminated too.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Headlight/Windshield Wiper Law'

questions.q: You must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
questions.explain: Pennsylvania requires low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving at Night'

questions.q: You must use low beams when following another vehicle within:
questions.explain: Use low beams when following a vehicle within 300 feet.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving at Night'

questions.q: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should look:
options: Toward the right edge of your lane
questions.explain: Looking to the right side of the road helps you avoid being blinded.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving at Night'

questions.q: In fog, rain or snow, you should use:
questions.explain: High beams reflect off fog or precipitation and reduce visibility.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Visibility Conditions'

questions.q: When must headlights be on in a posted work zone?
options: Only if the speed limit is reduced
At all times, day or night, in any posted work zone
questions.explain: Headlights are required in all posted work zones, not just active ones.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Work Zone Signs'

questions.q: If you are stopped for a traffic violation in a work zone without your headlights on, you face:
questions.explain: Failing to use headlights in a work zone adds a $25 fine.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Work Zone Signs'

questions.q: The most common type of crash in work zones is:
questions.explain: Double your following distance in work zones because rear-end crashes are most common.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Work Zones'

questions.q: In a work zone, you should:
options: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed
Slow down to watch the work
Stop to ask workers for directions
Not use cruise control and not cross a solid white line
questions.explain: Avoid cruise control, stay in your lane and keep moving at a safe speed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Work Zones'

questions.q: The Pennsylvania anti-texting law prohibits drivers from:
options: Sending, reading or writing text-based messages while the vehicle is moving
questions.explain: The texting ban covers text messages, instant messages and email; it is a primary offense.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Anti-Texting Law'

questions.q: What is the fine for a conviction under Pennsylvania's anti-texting law?
questions.explain: Texting while driving is a primary summary offense with a $50 fine.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Anti-Texting Law'

questions.q: Under Paul Miller's Law, which is prohibited while driving in Pennsylvania?
options: Holding a phone or other handheld device, even when stopped at a red light
questions.explain: The law bans handheld device use while driving, including temporary stops in traffic; hands-free use and emergency calls are allowed.
questions.ref: PennDOT news release on Paul Miller's Law (2026); 75 Pa.C.S. §3316.1

questions.q: Now that the warning period for Paul Miller's Law has ended (fines began in June 2026), a driver convicted of using a handheld device while driving pays a fine of:
questions.explain: Fines under the handheld-device ban began June 6, 2026, at $50 plus costs.
questions.ref: PennDOT news release on Paul Miller's Law (2026); 75 Pa.C.S. §3316.1

questions.q: Headphones or earpieces may be worn while driving:
options: In one ear only, for communication
In both ears if the volume is low
questions.explain: Only a single earpiece, in one ear, is allowed, and only for communicating.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving Distractions'

questions.q: Who must wear a seat belt under Pennsylvania law?
options: The driver, front-seat passengers, and all passengers ages 8 to 17 wherever they sit
questions.explain: Drivers and front passengers must buckle up; passengers 8–17 must be belted in any seat.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Seat Belt Law'

questions.q: In Pennsylvania, a child must ride in an approved child safety seat (not just a booster seat) until what age?
questions.explain: Children under 4 must be in a federally approved child safety seat, front or back.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Child Restraint Law'

questions.q: Children ages 4 through 7 must ride in:
options: An approved booster seat used with a lap and shoulder belt
Any seat with a lap belt only
questions.explain: Children 4 and older but under 8 must be in a booster seat.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Child Restraint Law'

questions.q: Children younger than 2 must ride in:
options: A rear-facing car seat until they outgrow its height and weight limits
A front seat with an airbag
questions.explain: Children under 2 must be secured rear-facing until they outgrow the seat's limits.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Child Restraint Law'

questions.q: Who is responsible for making sure children under 18 are properly restrained?
options: The child's parent only, even if not driving
questions.explain: Drivers are responsible for securing children and ensuring passengers under 18 are buckled.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Child Restraint Law'

questions.q: You should sit at least how far from the steering-wheel air bag?
questions.explain: Stay at least 10 inches away from the air bag.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Air Bag Safety Information'

questions.q: Which steering-wheel hand positions does the manual recommend?
questions.explain: 9-and-3 or 8-and-4 reduces overcorrecting and air-bag injuries.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Steering Your Way Out of an Emergency'

questions.q: In the penny test for tread depth, your tread is adequate if:
options: You can see all of Lincoln's head
Part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread
The tread reaches Lincoln's chin only
