questions.explain: Insert the penny head-first; if the tread hides part of Lincoln's head, there is enough tread.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Vehicle Checks: Preparing to Drive'

questions.q: When a tailgater is following you and there is no lane to move into, you should:
options: Gently tap your brakes and slowly reduce speed when the road ahead is clear
Move onto the shoulder at speed
questions.explain: Encourage the tailgater to pass by slowing gradually when it is safe.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Keep a Space Cushion Behind'

questions.q: If your vehicle breaks down on the highway, you should:
options: Stop in your lane and wait
Walk along the highway to find help
Pull as far off the road as possible, turn on hazard flashers and raise the hood
Leave it running in the right lane
questions.explain: Get off the road, use four-way flashers and lift the hood to signal a disabled vehicle.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Communicating Your Intentions to Other Drivers'

questions.q: If caught in fog so dense you cannot see, the best choice is to:
options: Pull completely off the road, turn on hazard lights, and wait
questions.explain: Pull off the road, preferably into a parking lot, until the fog clears.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Visibility Conditions'

questions.q: If snow or ice from your moving vehicle strikes another vehicle or person causing death or serious injury, you can be fined:
questions.explain: Clear all snow and ice before driving; fines are $200–$1,000 per offense.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Snow and Ice'

questions.q: Should you use cruise control on snowy or icy roads?
options: Yes, to keep a steady speed
questions.explain: Cruise control keeps applying power and can keep wheels spinning on slippery roads.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Snow and Ice'

questions.q: Black ice is most likely when:
options: The road is covered in fresh snow
The road looks wet but no spray comes from other vehicles' tires
questions.explain: A thin, clear layer of ice can look like wet pavement.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Snow and Ice'

questions.q: What is the best thing to do if you feel tired while driving?
questions.explain: The manual says the best response to drowsiness is to stop driving.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Lack of Sleep'

questions.q: Teen drivers are more likely to crash when they are driving:
questions.explain: Teens with teen passengers have a higher crash risk.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Driving Distractions'

questions.q: If you are pulled over by police at night, you should:
options: Search for your documents right away
Turn on your interior light and keep your hands visible
Get out and walk to the police car
Keep your engine running and radio on
questions.explain: Turn on the dome light, keep hands on the wheel and wait for the officer's requests.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'What to Do If You Are Stopped by the Police'

questions.q: A vehicle flashing only blue lights behind you is:
options: An ambulance requiring you to stop
questions.explain: Police lights are red and blue, or red only on unmarked cars; blue-only lights are not police.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'What to Do If You Are Stopped by the Police'

questions.q: Under the Move Over law, when approaching an emergency response area or a disabled vehicle marked with flares or signals, you must:
options: Move into a non-adjacent lane, or if you cannot, slow to at least 20 mph below the limit
questions.explain: Move to a lane not adjacent to the scene or slow to at least 20 mph below the posted limit.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: How many points are added for a Move Over law violation?
questions.explain: A conviction under the Move Over law adds 2 points.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: What is the maximum fine for a first Move Over law violation (with no injury)?
questions.explain: Maximum fines are $500 (first offense), $1,000 (second) and $2,000 (third or more), plus 2 points.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: Driving around a sign or barrier that closes a road for hazardous conditions such as flooding results in:
options: 2 points and a fine of up to $250 (up to $500 if responders are called)
questions.explain: You may also have to repay emergency response costs.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 5 (Laws and Related Issues), section 'Obedience to Traffic-Control Devices Warning of Hazardous Conditions Law'

questions.q: Before backing up, you should:
options: Rely on your backup camera only
Check behind the vehicle before getting in and turn your head to look through the rear window
questions.explain: Children and small objects are hard to see; do not depend on mirrors or sensors alone.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Looking Behind: Backing Up'

questions.q: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.explain: To maintain control on curves, slow down before entering.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Negotiating Curves'

questions.q: For drivers 21 and older, Pennsylvania considers you to be driving under the influence at a BAC of:
questions.explain: Adults are DUI at .08 BAC or more; erratic driving can lead to DUI at lower levels.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'What Constitutes a DUI?'

questions.q: For drivers under 21, the BAC level considered DUI in Pennsylvania is:
questions.explain: Under the Zero Tolerance law, drivers under 21 are DUI at .02 or more.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Zero Tolerance Law (Under 21 DUI)'

questions.q: The DUI 'High Rate' penalties apply to commercial vehicle drivers with a BAC of:
questions.explain: Commercial drivers at .04 or more face High Rate penalties.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 2 - High Rate'

questions.q: School bus drivers are subject to High Rate DUI penalties at a BAC of:
questions.explain: School bus drivers with .02 or more fall under Table 2.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 2 - High Rate'

questions.q: The 'High Rate' DUI category covers BAC levels of:
questions.explain: General Impairment is .08–.099; High Rate .10–.159; Highest Rate .16 and up.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Severe Penalties'

questions.q: The 'Highest Rate' DUI category applies to a BAC of:
questions.explain: Highest Rate is .16 and up, and also applies to test refusals and certain drug DUIs.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 3 - Highest Rate'

questions.q: Pennsylvania's Implied Consent law means:
options: By driving in Pennsylvania you have agreed to chemical testing if arrested for DUI
Police need a warrant for any test
You may refuse a test with no penalty
questions.explain: Being licensed to drive means you have agreed to breath or blood testing when lawfully requested.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: What happens to a first-time offender who refuses a chemical test after a DUI arrest?
options: A 1-year license suspension, even if later found not guilty of DUI
questions.explain: Refusal brings an automatic one-year suspension in addition to any DUI penalty.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: A driver with a prior DUI or refusal who refuses chemical testing faces a refusal suspension of:
questions.explain: With a prior, refusal brings 18 months, plus 18 more if convicted of DUI.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: Drivers who refuse a chemical test are penalized under which DUI table if convicted?
questions.explain: Refusing a chemical test places you in the Highest Rate penalty table.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 3 - Highest Rate'

questions.q: A driver under 21 convicted of a first DUI faces:
options: 2 days to 6 months in jail, a 1-year suspension and a $500–$5,000 fine
questions.explain: Under-21 DUI is punished at the High Rate level regardless of BAC.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Zero Tolerance Law (Under 21 DUI)'

questions.q: For a first-offense General Impairment DUI (.08–.099), the license penalty is:
questions.explain: First-offense General Impairment: 6 months' probation, $300 fine, no license action.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 1 - General Impairment'

questions.q: A first-offense High Rate DUI carries what license penalty?
options: 12-month suspension and 1 year of ignition interlock
questions.explain: Table 2 first offense: 12-month suspension and 1-year interlock.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 2 - High Rate'

questions.q: A driver with a BAC of .08–.099 who causes a crash with injury or property damage is penalized as:
options: Highest Rate only if a death occurs
questions.explain: Crashes with injury, death or damage move the driver to Table 2 penalties.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Severe Penalties'

questions.q: Under ARD for a first DUI offense, a driver may lose their license for up to:
questions.explain: ARD includes up to a 90-day license loss, evaluation, and Alcohol Highway Safety School.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'ARD Program'

questions.q: Which is the only thing that lowers your blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explain: Only time will sober you up.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Alcohol and Driving'

questions.q: According to the manual, one standard drink equals:
options: 12 oz. of regular beer, 5 oz. of wine, or 1.5 oz. of 80-proof liquor
questions.explain: These amounts contain about the same alcohol.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Alcohol and Driving'

questions.q: For a person under 21 in Pennsylvania, which is illegal?
options: Riding with an adult who drank earlier
Having alcohol in the vehicle they are driving
questions.explain: It is illegal for anyone under 21 to buy, consume, possess or transport alcohol.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Underage Drinking'

questions.q: Under Pennsylvania's underage drinking law, the fine for a person under 21 can be up to:
questions.explain: Courts may also require evaluation or alcohol education.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Underage Drinking'

questions.q: Driving under the influence of a non-prescribed Schedule I, II or III drug is punished at which level?
questions.explain: Drug DUIs fall under Table 3.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Table 3 - Highest Rate'

questions.q: PennDOT begins corrective action when a driving record reaches:
questions.explain: Corrective action starts at 6 or more points.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'The Pennsylvania Point System'

questions.q: How many points are removed from your record for each 12 consecutive months without a violation or suspension?
questions.explain: Three points are removed for each 12 violation-free months.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Point Removal for Safe Driving'

questions.q: When a driving record reaches 11 or more points, what happens?
options: The driver must retake the vision test only
questions.explain: At 11 points the license is automatically suspended; length depends on prior suspensions.
questions.ref: PennDOT fact sheet 'The Pennsylvania Point System' (March 2024)

questions.q: After a suspension is served and your driving privilege restored, your record generally shows:
questions.explain: Except in limited cases, a restored record shows five points.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Suspensions and Revocations'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for failing to stop at a red light?
questions.explain: Failure to stop for a red light is a 3-point violation.
questions.ref: PennDOT fact sheet 'The Pennsylvania Point System' (March 2024)

questions.q: Failing to comply with a lowered railroad crossing gate results in:
questions.explain: Ignoring a crossing gate or barrier brings a 30-day suspension.
questions.ref: PennDOT fact sheet 'The Pennsylvania Point System' (March 2024)

questions.q: Fleeing or attempting to elude police carries:
options: A 1-year suspension and a $500 fine, plus possible jail
questions.explain: Fleeing police is a serious offense with a one-year suspension.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Fleeing or Eluding Police'

questions.q: Which of these will result in suspension or revocation of your license?
options: Leaving the scene of a crash you were involved in
questions.explain: Hit-and-run, DUI, reckless driving, racing and fleeing police all lead to suspension or revocation.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Suspensions and Revocations'

questions.q: If your vehicle starts to skid because the rear slides left, you should:
options: Steer left, the direction the rear is sliding
questions.explain: Look and steer where you want to go; steer in the direction the rear is skidding.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If Your Vehicle Starts to Skid'

questions.q: While skidding, should you use the brakes?
options: No, braking makes the skid worse
questions.explain: Braking during a skid can lock the wheels and remove steering control.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If Your Vehicle Starts to Skid'

questions.q: In an emergency stop with anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should:
options: Press firmly and steadily without pumping
questions.explain: With ABS, keep firm continuous pressure; noise and pulsing are normal.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If You Have to Brake Suddenly'

questions.q: In an emergency stop without anti-lock brakes, you should:
options: Press and release the brakes repeatedly
questions.explain: Pumping helps prevent wheel lockup and skidding.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If You Have to Brake Suddenly'

questions.q: At speeds above about 25 mph, it is usually better to avoid a sudden obstacle by:
questions.explain: Steering reaction is faster than braking at these speeds, if you have good steering skills.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Steering Your Way Out of an Emergency'

questions.q: If you begin to hydroplane, you should:
options: Ease off the gas and keep the wheel steady
questions.explain: Slow down gradually so the tires regain grip; brake gently only if needed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Road Conditions: Hydroplaning'

questions.q: If a tire blows out, you should:
options: Hold the wheel firmly, stay off the brake and slowly ease off the gas
questions.explain: Braking after a blowout can cause a skid.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If You Have a Tire Blowout'

questions.q: If your accelerator sticks, you should first:
options: Shift to neutral and brake, keeping your eyes on the road
Reach down with your hand to free the pedal
questions.explain: Neutral removes power from the wheels; then steer off the road and stop.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If Your Accelerator Sticks'

questions.q: If you must turn off the ignition while moving in an emergency, why should you NOT turn the key to LOCK?
options: It will start the engine again
It will set off the airbags
It turns on the hazard lights
questions.explain: Turn to OFF, not LOCK, so you keep steering.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If Your Accelerator Sticks'

questions.q: If your right wheels drift off the pavement onto a lower shoulder, you should:
options: Ease off the gas, straddle the edge, then steer back gently when slow and clear
Speed up to climb the edge
questions.explain: Slow to under 25 mph (ideally about 10 mph) before easing back onto the road.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If Your Vehicle Drifts off of the Pavement onto the Shoulder'

questions.q: A vehicle is coming head-on in your lane. After honking, you should generally try to escape:
questions.explain: Swerving left risks a crash if the other driver corrects at the last moment.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If Another Vehicle is Approaching Head-On in Your Lane'

questions.q: How much water can cause you to lose control of a vehicle?
questions.explain: About six inches of water can make some cars stall or lose control; a foot of moving water can float many cars, and two feet can sweep away most SUVs and pickups.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Flooded Roadways'

questions.q: If your car stalls on railroad tracks and a train is coming, you should:
options: Stay inside with your belt on
Push the car off the tracks
Get out quickly and move away from the tracks
questions.explain: Leave the vehicle immediately and move as far from the track as possible.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: After a train passes at a crossing with more than one track, you should:
options: Go when the gate starts rising
Go as soon as the train clears
Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before crossing
questions.explain: Another train may be coming on a different track.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: When lights flash, a gate is down, a flagger signals, or a train sounds its warning or is close
questions.explain: Do not go around gates or ignore any signal of an approaching train.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 2 (Signals, Signs and Pavement Markings), section 'Railroad Crossing Signals'

questions.q: If you are involved in a crash, when must you call the police?
options: When anyone is injured or killed, or a vehicle must be towed
Only if you were at fault
questions.explain: Call police for injury, death or a vehicle needing to be towed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Crashes'

questions.q: If police do not investigate a crash involving injury, death or a towed vehicle, you must send a Driver's Accident Report (AA-600) within:
questions.explain: Send the AA-600 to PennDOT within five days.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Crashes'

questions.q: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. You should:
options: Drive away if damage is small
Leave a visible note with your name, phone number, date and time, and call police
questions.explain: Leave a note and report to police.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 4 (Driving Record Information), section 'Crashes'

questions.q: If your brakes fail in an older vehicle, one of the first steps is to:
options: Pump the brake pedal quickly and shift to a lower gear
questions.explain: Pumping can build pressure; then use the parking brake carefully if needed.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If You Have an Older Vehicle and Your Brakes Suddenly Fail'

questions.q: When using the parking brake to stop after brake failure, you should:
options: Hold the release so you can let off if the rear wheels lock
Pull it all the way at once
questions.explain: Holding the release lets you prevent a skid if the rear wheels lock.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'If You Have an Older Vehicle and Your Brakes Suddenly Fail'

questions.q: You come to a road covered by moving floodwater. You should:
options: Turn around and find another route
questions.explain: 'Turn Around, Don't Drown' - never drive into floodwater.
questions.ref: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95, rev. 4-21), Chapter 3 (Learning to Drive), section 'Floods'
